marketDemographics.source: Project Evergreen property OM (CBRE), Demographics page - 2025 current-year estimates
marketDemographics.note: A genuinely growing Atlanta MSA trade area: 5-mile population is up 23% since 2010 (77,338 to 95,125) and growing 1.18% annually, with the 1-mile ring growing 1.68% annually and households up 1.70%. The true trade area holds 228,293 people at $100,800 average household income with a 209,055 daytime population - the OM notes 56% of visitors travel more than five miles, consistent with a regional draw. Average household income is projected up 13-16% by 2030 across every ring.

deals.notes: READ THE NOI CAVEAT FIRST. Conyers Crossing is a 170,475 SF community center on approximately 15.14 acres with 825 feet of signalized frontage on Highway 138 just south of the I-20 interchange (167,000 VPD) in Conyers, Georgia, 20 miles east of Atlanta, built in 1978 and expanded in 1985. The marketed in-place NOI of $1,635,494 IS NOT WHAT THE CENTER EARNS TODAY. It rests on a PENDING, UNEXECUTED lease: CBRE models a National Fitness User at 46,573 SF and $14.00 PSF - $652,022 of base rent plus $154,063 of recoveries, or $806,085, which is 34% of the entire $2,378,168 of modeled tenant revenue - and its own note states the lease is pending and expected to open by early 2028 at the latest, while modeling the tenant as rent-paying from the start of the analysis for in-place NOI purposes. That space does not exist as leasable area yet either: it is carved out of Burlington's current 83,552 SF box through a right-sizing to 36,979 SF that ownership is still finalizing. The owner's actual YE-2025 income statement shows NET OPERATING INCOME OF $1,020,433 on $1,645,818 of total income. The 9/1/2026 rent roll shows in-place base rent of $1,011,066, or $5.93 PSF across 170,475 SF, with Burlington still occupying its full 83,552 SF at $2.11 PSF. So roughly $615,000 of the marketed NOI is contingent on two transactions closing. Mitigating that, CBRE states the seller plans to cover any gap rent, tenant improvements, landlord work and leasing commissions to the extent tenants are not yet rent-paying at closing - get that in the contract, because it is the difference between a 2.7% CAGR stabilized center and a lease-up deal. What is real is a strong location and two long-tenured anchors: Hobby Lobby (55,363 SF, 25 years at the center, $138 PSF sales at an 8% occupancy cost) and Burlington (24 years, 3% occupancy cost), both ranking above chain averages on Placer.ai, inside a regional retail node with Walmart, Home Depot, Kroger, Publix, Lowe's and Best Buy within a mile and nothing comparable for ten miles. The Burger King ground lease is a genuine hidden asset - 3,820 SF paying $66,500 with 47 years of tenure, a corporate lease, and CBRE marking it roughly 68% below market with three options to 2044 - and could be sold separately to reduce basis.
keyAssumptions: THE HEADLINE NOI IS PRO-FORMA, NOT ACTUAL. noi / effectiveGrossIncome / operatingExpenses carry CBRE's published In-Place Pro-Forma ($2,378,168 EGR less $742,674 of operating expense = $1,635,494) so this deal stays comparable with the rest of the library, which also carries OM-stated in-place NOI. But that figure INCLUDES $806,085 from a PENDING, UNEXECUTED lease (the National Fitness User at 46,573 SF and $14.00 PSF, being $652,022 of base rent plus $154,063 of recoveries - 34% of total tenant revenue). The owner's actual YE-2025 NOI was $1,020,433. Do not treat $1,635,494 as a going-in number without confirming both the fitness lease and the Burlington right-sizing are executed.

THE ROSTER IS THE ACTUAL 9/1/2026 RENT ROLL, NOT CBRE'S MODELED RECONFIGURATION. Per the standing rule that the rent roll is the final say on the roster, the 15 tenant rows here reflect what is actually leased today: Burlington in its full 83,552 SF at $2.11 PSF, F&D Barber Shop in suite B106, and NO fitness user. CBRE's model instead shows the post-reconfiguration state - Burlington at 36,979 SF, a 46,573 SF fitness user, B106 vacant, and a 589 SF unleasable mechanical/riser area that will only be created by the demising work. That is why totalSF here is 170,475 (the roll) rather than the OM's 171,064, and why occupancy reads 100% rather than 99%.

SOURCES: roster from the WHLR MRI rent roll dated 9/1/2026; options, recovery methods, the pending-lease disclosures, reported sales and occupancy-cost health ratios from the CBRE Argus model Project Evergreen_GA_Conyers Crossing (FINAL).xlsx dated 7/21/2026; historical income and expense from the WHLR income statement for the 12 months ended December 2025 (entity WHLRCC); demographics, traffic counts, parking ratio, Placer.ai rankings and property description from the property OM.

ROSTER TIE-OUT: 15 leases sum to 170,475 SF, exactly the rent roll's stated GLA (0 SF vacant, 100.0% occupied). Monthly base rent sums to $84,255.55, exactly the roll's printed total; annualized = $1,011,066. Monthly cost recovery sums to $34,301.68, exactly the roll's printed total; annualized = $411,621.

RECOVERIES BASIS DIFFERS FROM THE OTHER PROPERTIES IN THIS BATCH: nnnRecoveries and per-tenant expenseReimbursements come from the RENT ROLL here, not from CBRE's in-place table, because CBRE's per-tenant recoveries correspond to the post-reconfiguration roster (fitness user included, Burlington downsized) and cannot be matched to the actual roster. CBRE's modeled total is $717,411; the roll's actual is $411,621.

TWO TENANTS ARE LEASED BUT NOT YET PAYING RENT, and both are carried at $0 base rent so the roster ties to the roll: Caribbean Marketplace (1,050 SF, suite A102, rent commences 12/2/2026 at $28.00 PSF) and Pao Pao Ramen (3,825 SF, suite B102, rent commences 5/18/2027 at $24.17 PSF). CBRE describes Pao Pao as an executed lease with a projected rent commencement date. Both are flagged leaseStatus signed-not-open.

SUITE B106 CONFLICT - VERIFY: the 9/1/2026 rent roll shows F&D BARBER SHOP occupying 1,075 SF at $29.00 PSF on a lease running 11/1/2025 to 10/31/2030. The OM site plan and CBRE's model both show suite B106 as AVAILABLE and model a January 2028 re-lease at $27.00 PSF. Those cannot both be right. The roster follows the roll. Confirm whether F&D has vacated, is being bought out, or the OM is stale.
ACREAGE: the property OM states 15.14 acres; the VDR portfolio table states 15.16. Immaterial, but note the discrepancy.

WALT: 3.31 years on the actual roll as of 9/1/2026. CBRE reports 7.42 years, but that reflects the pending 10-year Burlington extension to December 2037 and the pending 10-year fitness lease - neither of which is executed. The VDR portfolio table's 2.8 is the anchor WALT. The gap between 3.31 and 7.42 is a good measure of how much of this deal is contingent.

ACTUAL vs PRO-FORMA EXPENSES: the owner's YE-2025 statement shows $625,386 of total operating expense against CBRE's $742,674 model. The 2025 actuals include $37,000 of one-time stormwater maintenance and $31,143 of bad debt expense - the highest bad-debt line in the batch, worth understanding. Real estate taxes ran $259,094 in 2025 versus CBRE's $272,920 modeled. CBRE explicitly did NOT reassess taxes and modeled them at 2026 budgeted amounts; Georgia counties reassess annually to fair market value, so a sale materially above the current assessment will flow through.

SALES BASIS: salesPSF and occupancyCost are CBRE's In-Place Pro-Forma reported sales and health ratios. Four tenants report; the rest are null rather than estimated. Note CBRE's sales columns for this property are partially column-shifted in the source file - the figures recorded here are the ones that reconcile against the OM's stated anchor health ratios (Burlington 3%, Hobby Lobby 8%).

CHIPOTLE IS NOT OWNED: an outparcel Chipotle sits on land the seller does not own, operating under a recorded REA through January 2068 and paying $5,280 a year of CAM contribution (the rent roll books it in the cost-recovery column, not base rent). It is carried as a 0 SF tenant marked isNAP so it does not distort GLA or rent metrics, with its CAM contribution preserved so recoveries tie to the roll.

LEASE CLAUSES ARE OM-SOURCED, NOT ABSTRACTED: the pending-lease terms, Burlington CAM structure and option schedules recorded in tenant notes come from CBRE's Argus lease summaries. The Burlington right-sizing amendment and the fitness lease should be reviewed in executed form before any of this NOI is underwritten.
NO PRICING: the portfolio is marketed unpriced, so askingPrice, capRate and pricePerSF are null rather than estimated.

redFlags.description: 34% OF THE MARKETED IN-PLACE REVENUE COMES FROM AN UNEXECUTED LEASE. CBRE's in-place pro-forma includes a Pending National Fitness User at 46,573 SF and $14.00 PSF, contributing $652,022 of base rent and $154,063 of recoveries - $806,085 of the $2,378,168 total. CBRE's own note reads: pending lease, expected to open by early 2028 at the latest; CBRE models tenant as rent paying at the start of the analysis for purposes of in-place NOI. The tenant is not in the 9/1/2026 rent roll, is not paying, and the space it would occupy has not been demised. If this lease does not sign, the marketed NOI does not exist.

The 46,573 SF the fitness user would occupy DOES NOT EXIST as separate leasable area today. It has to be carved out of Burlington's current 83,552 SF box through a right-sizing to 36,979 SF that ownership is still finalizing. CBRE states Burlington will remain open during construction, shifting over and back while a demising wall is built, with an estimated opening in the downsized space of late 2027 at the latest. That is construction risk, tenant-cooperation risk and timing risk stacked on top of leasing risk - and it also creates the 589 SF of unleasable mechanical/riser area the OM adds to GLA.

Actual NOI is roughly $615,000 below the marketed figure. The owner's YE-2025 income statement shows NET OPERATING INCOME OF $1,020,433 on $1,645,818 of total income and $625,386 of operating expense. The 9/1/2026 rent roll shows in-place base rent of $1,011,066 ($5.93 PSF), with Burlington still at its full 83,552 SF. Against CBRE's $1,635,494 in-place NOI, that is the size of the leasing and construction execution a buyer is underwriting. Note Burlington's rent also FALLS from $175,920 to $78,026 in the right-sizing, so the fitness user has to more than replace $97,894 of lost anchor rent before adding a dollar.

SELLER COVERAGE OF THE GAP IS THE KEY CONTRACT TERM. CBRE states: to the extent that tenants are not yet rent paying and/or any leasing costs are outstanding at closing, seller plans to cover any gap rent, TI, LL work and leasing commissions. That is the right structure and it substantially de-risks the pro-forma - but plans to is not an executed obligation. Get a specific, funded, escrowed seller obligation covering gap rent through rent commencement, all tenant improvement and landlord work costs for both the Burlington demising and the fitness build-out, and all leasing commissions. Without it, the NOI gap is the buyer's.

Suite B106 is shown two different ways. The 9/1/2026 rent roll has F&D Barber Shop in 1,075 SF at $29.00 PSF through 10/31/2030; the OM site plan and CBRE's model both show the suite AVAILABLE and model a January 2028 re-lease at $27.00 PSF. One of the two is wrong. If F&D is in fact leaving, that is a small additional vacancy; if the OM is stale, CBRE's lease-up assumption is double-counting income already in place. Resolve it in diligence.

Near-term anchor and box rollover. Burlington's CURRENT lease expires 3/31/2029 and Appliances 4 Less (3,500 SF, $51,380) expires 4/30/2027, within months of a closing with no options recorded. Hobby Lobby, 32% of GLA, expires 5/31/2030 with two options at $7.15 and $7.87 PSF - CBRE assumes exercise, and at $6.50 against a $14.00 PSF market rent that assumption is reasonable, but it concentrates 32% of the building in a single 2030 decision.

Mindy's Nails reports a 21% occupancy cost on $160 PSF sales - 2,100 SF at $26.46 PSF stepping to $29.78 by 2029. That is unsustainable for a nail salon, and the contracted escalations make it worse each year. The lease runs to 9/30/2030 with no options. Rainbow is also elevated at a 10% occupancy cost on $186 PSF sales across 8,640 SF.

Burlington's rent is $2.11 PSF - 85% below CBRE's $14.00 PSF market - and the pending deal keeps it there for another ten years. The right-sizing comes with a fresh 10-year term at the SAME $2.11 PSF through December 2037, plus four 5-year options at $8.00, $9.00, $10.00 and $11.00 PSF running to 2057. The OM presents the $8.00 first-option rent as driving cash flow growth and exit cap compression, but that step is eleven years away and everything before it is locked. Treat this as secure, sticky income on a 24-year-tenured anchor at a 3% occupancy cost - not as capturable mark-to-market.

Bad debt expense of $31,143 in 2025 - the highest in this batch and roughly 1.9% of total income. Combined with $2,259 of collection legal fees, it suggests real collection friction in the shop line. Ask for an aged receivable schedule.

GADOT's $85 million reconstruction and widening of the I-20 / Highway 138 interchange is IN PROCESS with completion planned for summer 2028. Long term this improves access to a center whose entire location thesis rests on that interchange. Through 2027 and into 2028, however, it means construction disruption on the primary access route during exactly the period the fitness user is meant to open and stabilize.

upsideItems.item: The fitness user, if it signs, transforms the asset
upsideItems.detail: 46,573 SF at $14.00 PSF with a 10% step to $15.50 in 2033 and four options running to 2057 at up to $22.69 PSF. That is $652,022 of base rent plus $154,063 of recoveries against a center currently producing $1,011,066 of total base rent. CBRE calls it a game-changing addition that should significantly increase traffic, and a fitness anchor is genuinely complementary to Hobby Lobby and Burlington rather than competitive. This is the deal - but it is an opportunity, not an in-place fact, and it should be priced as such.

upsideItems.item: Burger King ground lease - a separately saleable hidden asset
upsideItems.detail: 3,820 SF on a freestanding outparcel paying $66,500 of ground rent on a CORPORATE lease, with 47 years of tenure at the center (since April 1979) and three 5-year options at $73,150, $80,465 and $88,512 carrying it to 2044. CBRE marks it roughly 68% below market. The tenant self-maintains its building and the parking in front of it, and CBRE excludes its GLA from capital reserves. A separate sale at a ground-lease cap rate would be materially accretive against a community-center cap and would reduce basis - the OM explicitly flags this.

upsideItems.item: A dominant location inside a regional retail node, with public money going into the access
upsideItems.detail: 825 feet of signalized frontage on Highway 138 just south of an interchange carrying 167,000 VPD, with Walmart, Home Depot, Kroger, Publix, Lowe's, Best Buy, TJ Maxx, HomeGoods, Ross, Floor & Decor and Academy all within one mile and nothing of similar scale for ten miles. 1.6 million annual visits with 56% of visitors travelling more than five miles. GADOT's $85 million interchange reconstruction completes in summer 2028. Under the demographics-to-rent lens, a growing Atlanta MSA trade area (5-mile population up 23% since 2010, still compounding 1.18% annually, $100,774 average household income) with constrained competing supply supports pushing shop rents on rollover.

upsideItems.item: Two proven anchors with 24-plus years of tenure and excellent health ratios
upsideItems.detail: Hobby Lobby has been at the center since August 2001 and does $138 PSF at an 8% occupancy cost; Burlington since 2009 at the center (and per the OM 24-plus years of tenure) at a 3% occupancy cost. Placer.ai ranks Hobby Lobby in the top 48% and Burlington in the top 45% of their chains, and the OM states all other tracked tenants also rank above chain averages. Anchors average 11 miles to their nearest same-store location, which protects sales from cannibalization.

upsideItems.item: Genuine below-market rent across a shop line that rolls
upsideItems.detail: In-place rent averages $5.93 PSF against CBRE's $16.97 weighted-average market. Much of that gap is the locked anchors, but the shops are also below market with short terms: Appliances 4 Less at $14.68 vs $25.00 (expires 4/2027, no options), Rainbow at $10.59 vs $16.00, Republic Finance at $18.77 vs $27.00, Rose Couture at $24.40 vs $27.00. Nine of the fifteen leases carry contracted annual escalations already signed, including Pao Pao Ramen stepping from $24.17 to $37.84 by 2036.

upsideItems.item: Recent leasing momentum in the shop line
upsideItems.detail: Six leases commenced or renewed in the last eighteen months - Caribbean Marketplace (August 2026), Pao Pao Ramen (August 2026, an 11-year term), Rainbow (February 2026), F&D Barber Shop (November 2025), Mindy's Nails (October 2025), Republic Finance (October 2025) and Boost Mobile (July 2025). Whatever the pending anchor deals do, the small-shop market at this center is clearly active.

tenants.assumptionNote: Rent roll entity MCP STABLE - CHIPOTLE. NOT OWNED - CBRE labels this Chipotle (Not Owned) and marks it NAP. The outparcel sits on land the seller does not own; Chipotle contributes CAM under a recorded reciprocal easement agreement running to January 2068. Carried at 0 SF with $0 base rent so it does not distort GLA or rent-per-SF metrics, but its $5,280 annual CAM contribution IS preserved so recoveries tie to the rent roll's printed total (the roll books this amount in the cost-recovery column, not base rent). CBRE models $5,808 in its CY2027 in-place table. A Chipotle adjacent to the center is a traffic positive even though it pays no rent.
